title.en: The best material for a window

text.en:
Dev's school was building a new window. "Why not use wood?" asked a boy.
The teacher held a sheet of glass and a plank of wood to the light. Dev could see through the glass but not through the wood.
"A window must let light through," she said. "So we choose glass."

Everything around us is made of materials, such as wood, glass, metal, plastic, cotton and rubber.
We group materials by their properties. Appearance can be shiny (metals) or dull. Hard materials such as iron are hard to scratch; soft ones such as cotton or sponge can be pressed easily.
Transparent materials such as clear glass let light pass so we see clearly through them. Translucent materials such as butter paper let some light pass. Opaque materials such as wood and metal let no light pass.
Some materials dissolve in water. Sugar and salt are soluble. Sand and chalk powder are insoluble. Some things float on water and some sink.
We choose a material for its properties. Cooking pans are metal because metal is hard and heats up well. Windows are glass because glass is transparent.
Things are made of materials. We sort them by their properties, like hard or soft, shiny or dull.
Clear glass is transparent. Butter paper is translucent. A wooden board is opaque.
Sugar and salt dissolve in water. They are soluble. Sand does not dissolve. It is insoluble.
We pick a material by what we need. A pan is made of metal. A window is made of glass.

problem.en: Why is a cooking pan made of metal and its handle of plastic or wood?

text.en: The pan must be hard and must pass heat quickly.
The handle should not get hot in our hands.

why.en: Plastic and wood do not pass heat easily.

text.en: So each part uses the material with the right property.

prompt.en: Your friend wants a window made of a wooden sheet. What will you tell her?

requiredIdeas.en: A window must let light through.
Wood is opaque but glass is transparent, so glass is better.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking any hard material can be used for any job.

points.en: Materials are sorted by their properties.
Transparent, translucent and opaque describe how much light passes.
Soluble things dissolve in water; insoluble ones do not.
We choose a material for its properties.
